hero.title: Big taste for a
hero.lede: A capability-oriented control plane for self-hosted AI agents—with a real broker boundary, isolated custom tools, durable audit, and end-to-end OpenTelemetry on hardware you own.
hero.caveat: v0.2.0 ships 17 public Rust crates, three CLIs, a separate local broker, sandboxed model scripting, and OTLP traces + logs.

title: Small enough to own.
Serious enough to trust.
pillars.intro: Dekopon is no longer only an architecture sketch. Version 0.2.0 implements the hard seams: isolation, proposal-only clients, exact authorization, constrained host I/O, durable audit, and correlated telemetry.

items.title: Edge-sized by design.
items.body: Rust binaries, plain files, Unix sockets, Wasm components, and optional OTLP export. No required cloud control plane—and a real deployment already runs beside OpenObserve on a Raspberry Pi.

items.title: Permissioned by capability.
items.body: The runner can propose a named operation. Only the separately deployed broker can bind trusted identity, exact policy, HTTP limits, and a single-use authorization to execution.

items.title: Custom without tool sprawl.
items.body: The model sees one stable bash-shaped tool. Inside it, JSON-native scripts discover and compose operator-granted capabilities with loops, jq, pipelines, functions, and hard whole-session budgets.

items.title: Auditable and observable.
items.body: Hash-linked broker audit answers what was authorized. OTLP traces explain execution and latency. OTLP logs retain accounting, refusals, errors, and opt-in transcripts—correlated, not duplicated.

status.title: This is working software.
status.intro: The release is deliberately pre-production, but its maturity is concrete: published crates, provenance-attested binaries, strict protocols, end-to-end broker tests, and an OpenObserve smoke test in CI.

current.label: Current · unprivileged path
current.title: One model tool. Several bounded execution layers.
current.body: Run against an OpenAI-compatible endpoint or an isolated ChatGPT/Codex subscription, then let one sandboxed script compose direct and broker-backed capabilities.
points: Exactly one model-facing tool, regardless of capability count
JSON-native shell with control flow and real jq
No process execution, filesystem, or inherited environment
Fresh memory-, fuel-, time-, input-, and output-bounded Wasm stores
Chrome traces plus OTLP/HTTP or OTLP/gRPC export

direction.label: Current · authority path
direction.title: A separate broker that fails closed.
direction.body: dekopon-brokerd is a real Unix process with peer-UID authentication, exact deny-by-default policy, constrained async Wasm + HTTP execution, replay rejection, evidence, and durable audit.
direction.note: Intentionally not claimed yet: broker credential resolution, independently anchored checkpoints, a long-running agent daemon, or multi-tenant transport.

execution.title: One tool is an entire bounded plan.
execution.intro: A capability catalog should not inflate every prompt or force a model through one round trip per tiny operation. Dekopon exposes one replayable scripting surface and keeps every escape route closed.
execution.script:
items=$(cap --list)
for item in $items; do
  cap --describe $item | jq -c .inputSchema
done
execution.result: structured JSON values · bounded output · explicit exit codes

cards.title: Stable schema
cards.body: One tool definition stays constant as providers come and go. The model discovers only capabilities granted to this session through cap --list and cap --describe.

cards.title: JSON all the way down
cards.body: Variables are serde_json values. Pipelines pass structure rather than byte streams; flags become object fields; jq, arrays, maps, and arithmetic are native.

cards.title: A shell without the OS
cards.body: No subprocesses, filesystem, sockets, ambient environment, eval, exec, source, or glob expansion. curl only assembles a request for one granted capability.

cards.title: Budgets at every layer
cards.body: Steps, recursion, value memory, output, wall time, and capability calls bound the script; independent Wasmtime and broker ceilings bound each provider operation.

authority.title: A model may propose.
authority.intro: The client cannot smuggle identity, policy, constraints, credentials, or authorization over the wire. dekopon-brokerd derives trusted context from the connected peer and creates the non-cloneable authorization inside its own process.

nodes.title: Proposal
nodes.body: A capability ID, bounded JSON input, unique invocation ID, and trace context—no identity or grant fields.

nodes.title: Broker
nodes.body: Maps peer UID to trusted context, rejects replay, evaluates exact policy, and creates single-use authorization.

nodes.title: Provider
nodes.body: Runs in a fresh Wasmtime store. The host—not guest code—enforces exact HTTP authority, methods, bytes, call count, and deadline.

nodes.title: Evidence
nodes.body: Links identity, decision, effect class, sanitized call metadata, digest, and outcome in a verified audit chain.

invariants.title: Explicit and narrow
invariants.body: A read capability never implies write authority. The JSONPlaceholder demo gives GET and POST separate IDs and grants.

invariants.title: Identity from transport
invariants.body: Payloads have no principal or actor field. Local identity comes from Unix peer credentials plus owner-controlled mapping.

invariants.title: Authority stays behind the seam
invariants.body: The runner never receives AuthorizedInvocation, links privileged HTTP, or loads a component in explicit broker client mode.

invariants.title: Failure is actionable
invariants.body: broker-unavailable means no work began; outcome-unaudited means an effect may have happened and must not be retried.

observability.title: See the whole run. Keep the signals honest.
observability.intro: The runner exports OTLP traces and logs; the broker independently exports its correlated trace leg and writes structured JSON logs to stdout for an external collector. OpenObserve is the documented, CI-tested OTLP receiver—but any compatible backend can ingest the same signals.

signals.name: Broker audit
signals.question: What was authorized?
signals.body: Owner-only, append-synchronized JSONL with hash links, replay restoration, and a separately replaced count/head checkpoint.

signals.name: OTel traces
signals.question: What ran, where, and how long?
signals.body: Model turns, scripts, every executed command word, authorization, provider work, and sanitized HTTP calls form one cross-process trace.

signals.name: OTel logs
signals.question: What must survive a span?
signals.body: Runner OTLP logs retain token accounting, refusals, errors, and optional model/tool transcripts without noisy span mirrors; broker operational logs remain structured JSON on stdout.

observability.privacyTitle: Metadata by default. Payloads by explicit opt-in.
observability.privacyBody: Prompts, answers, scripts, tool output, provider input/output, URL paths and queries, headers, bodies, credentials, and raw errors stay out by default. Enabling telemetryPayloads widens selected proposal and transcript data, never headers, bodies, credentials, or durable audit.

measurement.label: Raspberry Pi · OpenObserve · physical allocation
measurement.title: for the current Dekopon signal sample
measurement.body: The dekopon streams used to exercise a simple prompt occupy 148 KiB of traces and 52 KiB of logs on disk. That is measured allocated space, not an apparent sparse-file size.
measurement.note: Snapshot: 16 Aug 2026. The whole OpenObserve stream tree was 1.22 MiB, including other streams and 860 KiB of index/metadata overhead. Values grow with ingestion; the PVC is not a hard quota.

resources.title: Declare capabilities in the open.
resources.intro: Compact, Kubernetes-inspired resources make an agent’s proposed authority inspectable. Unknown fields fail early. Names and references are validated before they enter the deterministic catalog.

points.label: api
points.title: Versioned on the wire
points.body: with explicit kinds and strict alpha schemas.

points.label: key
points.title: Symbolic credential references
points.body: keep real secrets out of authored resources.

points.label: sort
points.title: Deterministic ordering
points.body: keeps output stable for people and automation.

architecture.title: Coordination is not authority.
architecture.intro: Version 0.2.0 has two deliberately different execution paths. Direct mode is pure, import-free computation. Broker mode crosses a process boundary with a proposal and lets only the broker resolve privileged host I/O.

current.title: Typed local control
current.body: Strict catalog reads, deterministic output, and isolated model-account lifecycle.

components.title: Unprivileged runner
components.body: Model interaction, one scripting tool, and proposal-only broker client.

components.title: Authority broker
components.body: Trusted identity, policy, constrained execution, evidence, and durable audit.

components.title: Narrow provider
components.body: Fresh bounded store; only explicitly linked host interfaces exist.

roadmap.title: A strong foundation, without production theatre.
roadmap.intro: Dekopon v0.2.0 proves the local authority path. The next work strengthens credentials, rollback detection, and integration rather than pretending those concerns disappeared.

items.title: Typed local control
items.body: Strict resources, deterministic CLI, model clients, and import-free immediate providers.

items.title: Privileged local broker foundation
items.body: One-tool scripting, constrained async HTTP providers, exact policy, replay defense, durable audit, and cross-process OTLP.

items.title: Independent audit anchoring
items.body: Retain, sign, or remotely anchor checkpoint generations outside the broker host.

items.title: Broker-owned credentials
items.body: Destination-bound secret resolution only after redaction and authority constraints remain proven.

items.title: Unprivileged agent runtime
items.body: Connect operator resources and a future dekopond without moving effect authority out of the broker.

closing.title: Build agents that can act.
closing.body: The difficult boundaries are implemented, published, tested, observable, and ready for careful contributors—not hidden behind a roadmap slide.
